title: Staff velocity pricing feedback — sensitivity notebook
summary: Working notebook to explore how staff velocity (ramp speed, onboarding drag, churn), pricing adjustments, and SLA capacity interact under short bursts and sustained demand increases. Not a finalized model — quick sensitivity outputs, heuristic triggers, and recommended tactical mitigations for FY26 planning.
assumptions: average_throughput_per_engineer = 180 tokens/sec of steady-state optimization work (measures ops capacity improvement)
reserve_capacity_prepaid_buffer = 10% of peak qps by default
headline_findings: A 12% increase in effective price-per-token reduces required new hires for a +2x demand shock by ~28% in the 12-week window (holds other levers constant).
Onboarding lag is the dominant driver of short-term HC need; shortening to 4 weeks (via focused bootcamp) cuts urgent hiring needs by ~35% for burst scenarios.

Allocating a small prepaid burst reserve (5-8% of peak) smooths headcount spikes but increases unit cost by ~2-3 percentage points — worthwhile for predictable enterprise customers but poor for low-margin volume.
Mix changes (embedding-heavy vs. completion-heavy) shift token economics enough that per-route pricing or route-level quotas materially change hiring plan sensitivity.

Quantization and batching improvements we modeled (conservative ~10% token cost reduction) defer 2 hires in the mid-case over 26 weeks; more aggressive engineering gains are multiplicative with pricing changes.

hiring_triggers: SLA breach probability > 2% over rolling 7d -> immediate 2-week hiring cycle (contract-first).
Projected sustained token growth > 20% QoQ -> start ramp for permanent hires (hire plan horizon 12-16 weeks).
Reserve utilization > 70% for two consecutive weeks -> evaluate price increases or emergency contractor pool.
Customer commit upsell that covers >= 60% incremental unit cost -> prioritize dedicated capacity and delay hires.
pricing_sensitivity_notes: Method: blended unit-cost model combining GPU-hour, infra overhead, support SRE time allocated per token, and gross margin target. Sensitivities computed by reweighting demand mix across routes (embeddings vs completions), applying price deltas to revenue-per-token, and recomputing hires required to maintain latency SLOs using historical throughput-per-engineer heuristics. Model intentionally conservative on engineering improvements; run-specific numbers embedded below.
recommended_actions: Short term (0-12w): prioritize reserve procurement for high-value enterprise customers, open contractor pool, and run a 4-week onboarding acceleration pilot.
Medium term (12-26w): experiment with targeted price adjustments on low-margin routes rather than blanket increases; implement per-route quotas for free-tier customers to protect margin.
Long term (26-52w): invest in batching/quantization roadmap to reduce unit cost by 10-20%; model capex for dedicated clusters where margin justifies headcount savings.
Governance: add a weekly 'capacity delta' digest to finance-product standup with two simple KPIs: projected hires saved vs price change, and reserve-utilization trend.
